reconstructed_captions.31: Another piece of black material is carefully placed over the glued surface.
reconstructed_captions.32: A hand firmly presses the two pieces of material together, ensuring a strong bond.
reconstructed_captions.33: A hand uses a mallet and a stitching chisel to punch a line of holes in the leather.
reconstructed_captions.34: A close-up shows the prongs of the chisel creating evenly spaced stitching holes.
reconstructed_captions.35: The hand repositions the chisel to continue the line of holes along the edge.
reconstructed_captions.36: A hand begins saddle stitching with two needles, passing one through the first hole.
reconstructed_captions.37: The second needle is passed through the same hole from the opposite direction.
reconstructed_captions.38: The thread is pulled tight, creating a secure and neat saddle stitch.
reconstructed_captions.39: The hand continues the stitching process along the line of pre-punched holes.
reconstructed_captions.40: A close-up view highlights the uniform pattern of the hand-sewn stitches.
reconstructed_captions.41: After finishing the seam, the excess thread is cut with a small pair of scissors.
reconstructed_captions.42: A sharp craft knife trims the edges of the stitched leather pieces to be perfectly flush.
reconstructed_captions.43: A hand uses a sanding block to smooth the newly trimmed leather edge.
reconstructed_captions.44: An edge beveling tool is used to round off the sharp corners of the leather edge.
reconstructed_captions.45: A hand applies an edge finishing compound to the sanded and beveled edge.
reconstructed_captions.46: A wooden slicker is rubbed vigorously against the edge to burnish and seal it.
reconstructed_captions.47: A close-up shows the edge becoming smooth, dark, and glossy from the burnishing.
reconstructed_captions.48: A heated electric creasing tool is carefully guided along the edge of the black leather.
